I attached the PDF you sent and our internal usage-summary for reference. Can you confirm if this is a billing system error or if you need any documentation from our side? We need to reconcile this before we can post the invoice to our GL.

Thanks,

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:20:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on June invoice (VAT appears doubled)

Thanks for looping me in. Internal note: the £10k goodwill credit we issued on 2026-05-20 for the April performance regression was marked as VAT-inclusive in Zuora (billing metadata). That credit was applied line-item wise during invoice generation — I can confirm that's what landed on the June bill.

Given SkyFleet is a UK entity, if Finance issues a corrective credit that is VAT-exclusive it could leave them with a VAT accounting mismatch. Best to coordinate with Finance on whether they prefer a service credit (applied to next invoice) or an outright refund. Historically EU customers ask for credits since VAT on a credit note is simpler for their reclaim process.

I can offer a goodwill offset on their July invoice if Finance approves, but we should put the credit note through with clear VAT coding.

—Vanessa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

----
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Discrepancy on June invoice (VAT appears doubled)

Team — thanks for the context. I reviewed the posted invoice and the billing export. Notes: 1) The credit line was marked VAT-inclusive at issuance; 2) The invoice template re-applies VAT at the subtotal level if the invoice has any VAT-applicable line items — our billing engine doesn’t automatically net VAT from previously VAT-inclusive credits. That produced the duplication.

Recommendation (compliant + least operational friction):
- Issue a VAT-corrected credit note for £3,200 (net and VAT lines separated) dated 2026-06-30, with VAT amount explicitly zeroed on the original credit line and the correct VAT on taxable lines.
- Apply the credit note to SkyFleet’s account so it reduces their balance; the credit will appear on their next invoice (July).
- If SkyFleet requires cash refund instead, Finance can process a refund after receiving a formal request from AP; note that refunds will require a short KYC/payment verification and may be delayed by bank processing (5–7 business days).

I’ll draft the credit note and the VAT memo for their records. Vanessa — can you confirm SkyFleet will accept a credit on the next invoice? Elena / AP — please confirm if you prefer a cash refund instead.

Marissa Cole
Senior Accounting Manager, Redwood Inference
